title: Skill: revalidate-done-tasks — non-blocking findings from PR #93's review
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #93 (skill-revalidate-done-tasks-followups), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: `.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md`'s 'Handling a task that no longer holds' step 1 (same-day audit-branch collision handling) contains a self-contradictory sentence: "If its PR was already merged or closed, the name is free to reuse for a new, unrelated run — fall back to a numeric-suffixed name instead". The first clause says the name is free to reuse; the second immediately instructs *not* reusing it but falling back to a numeric suffix instead. The actionable instruction (use a numeric suffix) is clear enough to follow, but the preceding clause is confusing and should be reworded or dropped so a future reader/agent isn't left wondering whether literal reuse or suffixing is actually intended.

`.claude/skills/revalidate-done-tasks/SKILL.md`'s same-day audit-branch collision handling (step 1 of 'Handling a task that no longer holds') only covers two cases for an existing same-day `audit/revalidate-<YYYY-MM-DD>` branch: one with an open PR (reuse it) and one whose PR was merged/closed (fall back to a numeric suffix). It doesn't address a branch of that name existing (locally or on `origin`) with *no* PR at all — e.g. a prior run that cut the branch but crashed or was interrupted before pushing/opening a PR. Add explicit handling for this case (e.g. treat it the same as the merged/closed case and fall back to a numeric suffix, or reuse the abandoned branch after confirming it's genuinely stale) so the collision-handling logic is exhaustive.
